articleTitle: Comparative Study Between Two Modes of Control on a Lab Developed BLDC Motor Prototype
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: This paper presents the implementation of both closed loop trapezoidal and sinusoidal modes of control of a generic permanent magnet AC machine (PMAC) on a existing lab developed Brush-less DC (BLDC) prototype, of ratings 0.75 HP, 1500 RPM. The control strategies are modelled and simulated in standard available software packages and then implemented practically on the above mentioned BLDC prototype. The study is aimed at two subtle yet very significant goals, viz (i) the possible dynamic changeover between the two modes during quadrant transitions in drives applications and (ii) develop a simple approach towards identification of the type of PMAC machines as BLDC or PMSM which are apparently otherwise similar almost in all respect if nameplate details are absent. Both the simulation and experimental results are compared and are found to be in good agreement.

articleTitle: Optimal Placement of Distributed Generation for Minimization of Power Loss, Carbon Emission and Voltage Deviation Considering Demand Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Optimal position of Distributed Generation has been obtained in an unbalanced radial distribution system with lateral branches where loads are probabilistically varying in nature. Here four single objective indices like expected value of mean voltage, efficiency of distribution network, profitability index (PI) and Certified Emission Reduction (CER) and one multi-objective function giving priority to first two indices are set as decision making factor on yearly basis. Results obtained for different indices have been compared for IEEE 34 node test feeder.

articleTitle: Simulation and Modelling of Multi-Bounce Impulse Responses of Indoor Visual Light Communication Link for Any Arbitrary Optical Transmitter and Receiver Positions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: This article introduces a method that uses 3D CAD models to simulate the impulse response of the channel used in visible light communication inside a confined environment of a room for varying wavelengths utilizing a Monte Carlo ray-tracing approach.

articleTitle: i -Honk: Self Honk Detection from Smartphone Sensing for Driver Personalization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Densification in traffic day by day leading to increase noise pollution and which may be the potential health issues on the local level<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S016041202300140X. One of the main causes of traffic congestion is the rapid growth of two-wheeler and four-wheeler particularly in emerging countries. We need driver profiles in order to take appropriate action based on honking in addition to good urban planning in order to control noise pollution. In this study, we use deep learning method to develop a smartphone-based self-honk detecting system based on two-wheeler. Here we have created two models, one for self-honk and ambient noise detection in controlled environment and another will classify self-honk, ambient honk and ambient noise in realtime environment. Here we get some useful results making the system into two models. In a controlled setting, Model 1 provides 98% training accuracy and 96 % testing accuracy in honk detection. In contrast, Model 2 has been trained in realtime using self-honk data, ambient noise, and ambient honk, and it provides 85 % training accuracy and 82 % testing accuracy.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of Serial Peripheral Interface Transceiver Module
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: The design and simulation of a Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI) transceiver module using VHDL is being dealt with in this paper. SPI, a widely used communication protocol for communicating between micro-controllers and peripheral devices, is being utilized. VHDL (VHSIC Hardware Description Language), a hardware description language, is used for modelling digital circuits and systems. The work involves designing the SPI transceiver using VHDL and simulating it using a hardware simulator to ensure proper functionality. The design has been implemented on an FPGA board, and the performance of the SPI transceiver is being evaluated in terms of speed and power consumption. Overall, this paper contributes to the field of digital design by offering a FPGA-based solution for SPI communication, providing a foundation for the development of reliable and efficient embedded systems.

articleTitle: Software Cost Estimation: A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: One of the most crucial aspects of software development is software cost estimation. It entails calculating the amount of time and money needed to finish the software development. Software cost estimation is crucial when a project's lines of code surpass a certain threshold and when the programme is released with too many errors and unmet criteria, which results in the project being abandoned. The calculation of software costs for a project is a critical factor in determining whether or not its development is approved. Numerous approaches for estimating software costs have been implemented. The timely and cost-effective completion of software is ensured by appropriate cost estimation. The conclusion is that there isn't a single strategy that works well in every situation or for every job. Therefore, in order to compare all approaches and determine which one is the best and most likely to produce realistic and accurate estimations, a complete understanding and rigorous analysis are needed. This article discusses the process of determining the most accurate approach for software cost estimation in order to provide higher levels of accuracy.

articleTitle: Time-Varying Linear Quadratic Control of Modular Multilevel Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: In the past few years, the modular multilevel converter (MMC) has seen extensive application in the high voltage sector. The MMC is composed of multiple similar submodules (SMs). In order to ensure the optimal functioning of the Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC), it is imperative to maintain a balance between the voltages of the upper and lower arms of the capacitor. Additionally, it is essential to suppress the alternating current (AC) components of the circulating current. Due to the complex interdependence of the equations governing the dynamics of the MMC, the control of MMC systems becomes complicated. This study presents a control methodology that aims to provide stable and balanced operation, while minimizing the ac components of the circulating current. In this study, the time-varying linear-quadratic control approach that has time-varying feedback gains for achieving stable and voltage-balanced operation while simultaneously decreasing the ac components of the circulating current. The simulations were performed on a single-phase half bridge MMC with 10 SMs. The results of both the theoretical study and the simulation are provided and discussed here. The simulation results confirm the efficacy of the suggested control approach.

Author Keywords: Linear time variant system Modular multilevel converter

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Identification Using a Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: The health of people is seriously threatened by brain tumours, and the prognosis of patients is greatly enhanced by early identification. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have demonstrated impressive performance in a range of computer vision applications, such as the processing of medical images. This work proposes an effective brain tumor detection system using the VGG16 (Visual Geometry Group 16-layer) CNN architecture. A dataset of brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans is used by the proposed system to identify characteristics of the existence of tumors. Utilizing pre-trained weights on ImageNet, transfer learning is used to improve the model's performance. Our results found VGG16 model is a good option for precisely identifying brain tumors from MRI images. As a dependable instrument for early diagnosis, the proposed system has promise for improving patient care and neuroimaging results.

articleTitle: Design, Fabrication, Performance Comparison and Studies on Buck Converters for Determining Frequency Limits of Soft Commutation Failure
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: This paper presents the design, analysis, fabrication and experimental results of a DC-DC Buck converter switching at 100 kHz, incorporating both zero current switching (ZCS) & zero voltage switching (ZVS). An experimental prototype has been developed in the laboratory to test the converters. The selection of the resonating elements has been done to conduct successful ZC turn-off and ZV turn-on at 100 kHz. The studies on soft switching commutation failure conditions for both ZV and ZC switching have been presented with respect to different loss figures and analysed. Further, a comparative study has been presented for hard, ZC and ZV switchings to select the most suitable scheme for a particular operating condition. The thermal performance of the switching devices, for these switching schemes have also been studied to validate the same.

articleTitle: Intelligent Analysis and Identification of Palm Gestures using ML Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: The area of human-computer interaction (HCI) has made significant strides in recent years, thanks in large part to the development of innovative technologies that aim to improve the way in which people and machines work together. One of these areas is the use of hand gestures to control gadgets and apps, which has the potential to create a form of interaction that is more intuitive and natural. The introduction of a palm gesture detection system that is both dependable and effective has the potential to completely alter the ways in which we interact with various electronic gadgets and software programmes. The objective is to develop a palm gesture recognition system that is capable of precise detection and classification of hand gestures in real time. The computer vision methods is applied to collect and interpret the hand movements. Following this, machine learning algorithms will be used to train the system on a huge dataset consisting of hand gestures. The system will be able to identify the hand gestures in real time and will categorise them according to predetermined categories. The experimental results are compared against other gesture recognition systems to study the accuracy of the system.

articleTitle: On-Load Parameter Estimation of Inductors in DC-DC Buck Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: This paper presents the design, fabrication and testing of an EE-shaped ferrite core based inductor in a lab-developed synchronous buck converter prototype at 30 W @ 200 kHz. The main aim is to propose an accurate analytical method to calculate the AC resistance of the inductor winding at different frequencies and segregate core and copper losses. The flux linkage associated with the coil is estimated to calculate the operating flux density. A study has been conducted to decide the approximation required for the harmonic expansion of the inductor current waveform. The results are further validated through on-load experiments. The on-load inductance has also been calculated from the experimental flux linkage vs current curve. The effect of temperature has been taken into account during the analysis. Excellent agreement between the experimental and analytical/ simulated results uphold the accuracy of the analysis and precision of the experiments.

articleTitle: Highly Selective Triple Band Filter Using Stub Loaded Folded Step Impedance Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: A triple pass band filter with central pass band frequencies 2.4, 5.2 and 8.6 GHz is proposed in this article for the application in Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) and Satellite Communication. The impedance ratio of a pair of Folded Step Impedance Resonator and the positioning of a pair of open stubs are accurately adjusted to achieve these pass band frequencies. Apart from these another pair of open stubs are used to produce multiple Transmission zeros in between the pass bands. The simulation of the proposed filter is done with HFSS13 software and the measured frequency response of the fabricated prototype achieved high correlation with the simulation results. The miniaturized size of the filter is (20.7mm x 22mm) and the in-band Insertion Losses are 0.8, 1.0 and 0.9 dB.

articleTitle: AI's Influence on Cinematic Restoration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: The Aesthetics of Old Film Formats explores the dynamic interplay between traditional cinematic aesthetics and the transformative impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on the revitalization of vintage film formats. The emergence of AI technologies has breathed new life into the world of cinema, fostering a renaissance of classic film formats such as 8mm, 16mm, and 35mm. Filmmakers and visual artists now have access to AI-powered tools and algorithms that can restore, enhance, and creatively manipulate analog footage, offering a bridge between the past and the future. This paper examines how AI, with its ability to upscale, colorize, and refine aged film material, has preserved cinematic heritage and extended the horizons of creative expression. There is a research gap in understanding the complex ethical implications and difficulties associated with the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the preservation and manipulation of analog footage, even though the abstract emphasizes the transformative impact of AI on the revival of vintage film formats. Authenticity, historical accuracy, and the possibility of unintentional biases created during the AI-driven restoration and augmentation procedures are some examples of ethical considerations. The abstract also emphasizes how AI might help preserve film history and foster new forms of artistic expression.

Author Keywords: AI Tools Analog films to digital Alteration
Impact of AI in Film Restoration

articleTitle: Modelling and Control of a Flexible Link Rotary Servo
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: This work presents a study on the modelling and control of a flexible link rotary servo. The lab-scale apparatus, consisting of a flexible link attached to the Rotary Servo Work Station, is analyzed using mathematical models derived from fundamental laws of physics. A state variable model is developed and utilized for the design of a Linear State Variable Feedback (LSVF) controller. The designed controller is physically applied to the system. To further enhance the control performance,a parametric uncertainty is included in the system and a robust LSVF controller is designed. Finally a neural network-based PID controller is designed for the same system. The closed-loop responses are compared with that of the traditional PID controller (designed via MATLAB PID toolbox), demonstrating the effectiveness of the neural network control strategy in achieving improved system performance.

articleTitle: Transient Analysis of MGMC Spark Gap Switches for Improved Performance in Pulse Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: This paper deals with detailed investigations on the switching behaviour of planar Multi-gap, multichannel (MGMC) spark gap switches that influence their performance in pulse power systems for generation of high magnitude (≥100 kA), fast-rising (≤1 μs) current pulses. The switching behaviour of these switches were studied using a transient equivalent circuit model developed for a 5-gap, planar, air-operated MGMC switch. The coupling parameters between the various switch components were determined using 3-D Electrostatic FEM simulation of the switch geometry using COMSOL Multiphysics 6.0®. Effect of position of trigger electrode on the overall switching performance was studied. Additionally, the effect of adjacent ground plate on the coupling parameters of the switch and the effect on its overall switching behaviour was studied in detail as part of this analysis. Studies reveal that application of negative-polarity trigger pulse on intermediate electrodes just adjacent to the high-voltage (HV) or ground electrodes result in maximum over-volting, thereby causing faster closing time and lesser switching jitter. Also, the incorporation of an adjacent ground plate reduces the overall “sensitivity” of the switch electrodes to the trigger pulse, thereby resulting in much greater over-volting. Thus, the transient analysis of planar MGMC spark gap switches using equivalent circuit model provide important insight into the switching behaviour of these switches which can be utilized to achieve faster rise-time, low-jitter and fast closing times.

articleTitle: Suddh Salil - An Automative Waste Management Technology Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: In the era of pollution water being a resource we cannot waste. India is a country of agriculture and the need of water is high yet surface water is polluted thus cannot be used. Many water resources like ponds and small lakes in the village or urban area cannot be used just because the resources are not clean enough. Cleanliness is much needed; this is where the proposed model “Suddh Salil” comes into play its role. The proposed model will take out any kind of floating waste product from the surface of stagnant water. Cleaning of surface water by traditional way was to make people get in the water and retrieve the waste products. This procedure is time consuming as well as not very precise. This proposed model will clean the surface of any stagnant water resource with the help of machine learning algorithm. Thus, making the cleaning process more precise and with automation. The model can precisely clean upper surface of the stagnant water resource using panoramic vision algorithm, YOLO V7(You Only Look Once) and Support Vector Machine (SVM).

articleTitle: Process Variation Impact on Dual Dielectric Gate-All-Around Tunnel FETs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: During fabrication of cylindrical gate-all-around (GAA) structure, the probability of getting uneven radius is highly probable which result in significant changes from its predefined performance expectations. In this work, a III-V GAA structure has been used. In addition, high-k gate dielectric has been employed close to source-to-channel junction and low-k gate dielectric has been used closed to drain-to-channel junction to enhance the tunneling efficiency and reduction in ambipolar current (IAmb). The analog/RF FoMs have been analyzed for probable variation in radius with variation in device geometry during fabrication. The cylindrical GAA counterpart has been compared with elliptical variation in their geometry i.e., aspect ratio of 0.5. The device has been further compared with fully channel low-k dielectric and high-k dielectric. The optimized structure, analog, and RF figures-of-merits are evaluated to get a clear understanding of such variations.

articleTitle: Design and Development of DC Bias Filter for Solid State Oscillator at W-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: This paper describes the design and development of DC Bias Filter for waveguide structure solid state diode oscillator at W band. It is a co-axial filter having alternative low and high impedance elements which prevents RF energy transmission at oscillator fundamental frequency around 92–96 GHz and 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> harmonic frequency through the DC bias circuit. The goal is to design DC bias filter with cut off frequency of 52 GHz and optimize its s-parameter using commercially available 3D EM software like CST Microwave studio. The filter has been fabricated and is used to bias pulse diode oscillator in WR 10 waveguide cavity. A Novel technique is used to calculate the value of line impedance and corresponding width and length of the filter section as the empirical formula used at low frequency is not valid at millimeter wave frequency.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Diverse Architectures for Accurate Blood Cancer Cell Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Blood cancer cell diagnosis is crucial in medical diagnostics. It demands accurate classification of blood cell images. Proper classification of blood cancer cells is fundamental for accurately diagnosing the specific type and subtype of blood cancer as well as efficient treatment planning. It provides specific information, helping healthcare professionals predict the prognosis, survival rates, and the potential for disease recurrence. On this basis, deep learning models have demonstrated remarkable performance. In this paper, we have introduced a comprehensive research into blood cancer cell classification, employing a diverse dataset encompassing various blood cell types. We explore the effectiveness of VGG19 with batch normalization, Vision Transformer (ViT), Ensemble Adversarial Inception-ResNetV2, DenseNet201, and ResNeXt50 architectures in this challenging task. In order to enhance the model performance, we integrate essential data preprocessing techniques, including resizing, cropping, and normalization. Additionally, novel data augmentation strategies, such as random cropping, and flipping are introduced to augment the training dataset and improve model generalization. Remarkably, VGG19 with batch normalization has shown tremendous success by achieving 99.86% accuracy. Moreover, the DenseNet201 model has performed brilliantly by achieving an accuracy of 98.55%. The ResNeXt50 model shows excellent performance with an accuracy of 98.31%. The Vision Transformer (ViT) achieves a solid accuracy of 98.91%. Lastly, Ensemble Adversarial Inception-ResNet V2 also performed no-tably achieving 96.38%. In this context, VGG19 with batch normalization is able to show more excellent performance than other models by achieving the highest accuracy.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis Between Deep Learning and Machine Learning Algorithms Based on User Review Sentiment Analysis from Various OTT Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: The golden period of television has moved to the screen in our hands, as streaming in the era of OTT(over-the-top) platforms. However, among OTT users, disengagement and platform churn are becoming more frequent. This study examines sentiment analysis in the context of OTT content through a comparative analysis of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models on user reviews from the Google Play Store and Apple App Store. We analyzed 56,351 user reviews from ten popular OTT apps, classifying them as positive (21,446), neutral (19,120), and negative (15,785). Preprocessed and feature-extracted data was fed to both ML models (Logistic Regression, XGBoost, etc.) and DL models (BiLSTM, LSTM, CNN). All of these are capable of extracting textual characteristics and insights from datasets and are also used to capture complex sentiment nuances in user reviews. BiLSTM, a deep learning algorithm, surpassed all other models, achieving an astounding 92% accuracy compared to Logistic regression, which achieved 66.62% accuracy and was the best-performing machine learning model in capturing user sentiment.

articleTitle: Automated Texture Feature Based Bone Tumor Segmentation and Image Analysis Using Supervised Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Manual demarcation of tumors in MR Images is time consuming, hard to reproduce and prone to intra rater variability. Accurate tumor demarcation is required for diagnosis and prognosis of tumors and in quantitative image analysis techniques like Apparent Diffusion Coefficients (ADC) using diffusion weighted (DW) MRI. In this study, fully automated machine learning algorithms were developed using textural features extracted from multimodal MRI. A total of 20 patients (n=20; Male:Female=16:4; Age=15.5±2.6 years) with biopsy proven osteosarcoma were analyzed. Multimodal MRI dataset including T1, T2 and proton density weighted MRI and DW-MRI were acquired before treatment using 1.5 T Phillips Achieva MRI scanner. 15 textural features were extracted using Grey-level co-occurrence matrices and Grey-level run length matrices in tumor volume from multimodal MRI. Four fully automated supervised machine learning algorithms 1) Logistic Regression, 2) Linear Support Vector Machines (L-SVMs), 3) Random Forests, and 4) Gradient Boosted D-Trees (GBDTs) were implemented and tested using accuracy metrics as dice coefficient (DC), precision, recall and accuracy. The ADC values calculated in manually demarked and segmented tumor volume were compared for clinical reliability. Logistic Regression demonstrated the best performance (DC: 0.70±0.12; precision: 0.72±0.18; recall: 0.74±0.19; accuracy: 0.98±0.02); While Random forest and GBDTs showed comparable performance (DC: 0.68±0.14, 0.68±0.14; precision: 0.73±0.19, 0.71±0.20; recall: 0.73±0.22, 0.75±0.22; accuracy: 0.98±0.02, 0.98±0.02 respectively); and L-SVM showed comparatively inferior performance (DC: 0.61±0.16; precision: 0.63±0.20; recall: 0.74±0.24; accuracy: 0.97±0.03) than the other methods. The masks segmented by four methods have ADC values ((1.17–1.21)x10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/sec) similar to those of manually demarcated masks (1.27×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/sec) and can be used for tumor assessment in clinical settings. Therefore, proposed segmentation methods showed clinically acceptable accuracies and considerable reduction of manual effort involved.

articleTitle: An Effective EEG-Based Image Classification Methodology Under Low Data and Resource Requirements Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Deep Learning (DL) methods such as Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) learning approaches are used to extract features from images through convolution operation. These features are widely used for image classification, object detection or segmentations tasks. But a high testing accuracy needs lot of input images for training, whereas a human brain can do similar tasks with a few training samples. Present study is aiming to establish the potential of extracted features from electroencephalogram (EEG) signals acquired from brain superior to CNN extracted features for image classification tasks. For this, EEG signals are collected while seeing an image and thinking about its attributes through a questionnaire. A five-channel EEG headset has been used for data collection. Four standard statistical features, namely mean, standard deviation, kurtosis and skewness have been extracted from signals emitted from each electrode. A total of twenty features extracted from five-channel EEG data have been used as input in training against the output labels through four different machine learning (ML) classifiers such as random forest (RF), support vector machine (SVM), multi-layer perceptron (MLP), extreme gradient boosting algorithm (XGBoost). Same images have been used for training, and inferenced through a CNN based binary classifier. Results show a lower performance metrics with CNN than EEG feature-based classifiers. Such concept can overcome the high data related constraint in areas like manufacturing.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Analysis of IoT Healthcare Data- A Review of Contemporary Research
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: One of the prime technological advancements in modern healthcare solutions is smart and interconnected wearable devices. The progress of the Internet of Things (IoT) has facilitated the ability of wearable devices to gather data on an unprecedented magnitude. Managing and utilizing such a substantial volume of data produced by healthcare equipment within the IoT framework is a formidable challenge. The utilization of IoT healthcare data for information mining, knowledge extraction, and disease prediction has garnered considerable interest in recent times. In recent times, Machine Learning has emerged as a prominent field of study that has effectively addressed a range of problems in IoT like big data analysis, networking challenges, energy efficiency, resource allocation, and security. This paper provides a detailed assessment of the application of machine learning techniques for addressing different challenges in the IoT-based healthcare industry. In addition, this work highlights a comparison of the strengths and weaknesses of current methodologies.

articleTitle: Photometric Invariant Visual Walking Stick Detection in Human-Robot Coexisting Environments: A Stratified Random Sampling Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: This work focuses on solving a crucial problem within the genre of human-robot coexistence, that is, accurate detection of a walking stick held by the human target in the series of visual images acquired by the onboard vision sensor of a mobile robot, during people following. Considering that the stick poses are subjected to various transformations during the tracking process, this study demonstrates how the stick detection problem can be solved as a general-purpose template matching problem. A high-speed randomized template matching algorithm, namely FAsT-Match, which is designed for approximate template matching under 2D affine transformations, has been effectively implemented in our work of walking stick detection. However, the matching performance of the FAsT-Match degrades when the real-life stick images get affected by photometric variations. Moreover, keeping in mind the real-life applicability of the algorithm, only a minor fraction of pixels is scanned from the images at random for the evaluation of the fitness of individual transformations, and the degree of randomness influences the matching outcomes. The present study proposes an improved adaptation of the FAsT-Match for walking stick detection in photometrically affected human-robot coexisting environments, called stratified sampling based photometric invariant affine template matching (SS-PIATM). The proposed approach offers a robust solution in the face of photometric variations, as well as improves the matching accuracy by introducing a new stratified random-sampling based mechanism for the evaluation of affine transformations. Real-life performance evaluations aptly demonstrate the supremacy of the proposed SS-PIATM algorithm in walking stick detection during human following with a mobile robot. *

articleTitle: Automatic Eyeblink Artifact Removal from Single Channel EEG Signals Using One-Dimensional Convolutional Denoising Autoencoder
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Eyeblink artifacts are common and significant disruption that occurs when the subject blinks during the recording of the Electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. Removing this artifact is essential to ensure the precision and reliability of the recorded brain activity. Compared to multichannel EEG systems, the limited spatial resolution of single channel EEG makes it more challenging to identify and eliminate eyeblink artifacts. In this work, we proposed a one-dimensional Convolutional Denoising Autoencoder (CDAE) architecture to efficiently remove the eyeblink artifacts from the single channel EEG signals. The publicly available “EEGdenoiseNet” dataset was used to synthetically generate the eyeblink-contaminated noisy EEG signals which were fed to the encoder to generate a compressed representation and capture essential features. From there, the decoder reconstructed the clean EEG signal. We calculated the Relative Root Mean Square Error (RRMSE) and Correlation Coefficient (CC) to assess the effectiveness of our proposed method and achieved an RRMSE of 35.4% and CC of 0.92. Our proposed method efficiently removes eyeblink artifacts from the single channel EEG signal and performs better in terms of CC compared to any other state-of-the-art method.

articleTitle: RGSO-Based Energy-Efficient Clustering for Sustainable IoT Using Dynamic Voronoi Diagram
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Sustainable IoT specifies the idea of combining IoT technologies in such a manner that reduces ecological impact, enhances resource productivity and encourages prolonged sustainability. Various considerations are there to create IoT sustainability such as energy efficiency, network efficiency, scalability, data security, optimizing resource uses, monitoring etc. With this perspective, deploying the sensor nodes for sustainable IoT and incorporating an energy-efficient clustering method for data transmission to make IoT sustainable. From various research works, it is found that cluster-based routing addresses this issue efficiently, still, some scopes are there for improving the network's performance to select optimal Cluster Head considering some major parameters. The meta-heuristic techniques show some promising results for improving the network's performance in recent research. In the proposed mechanism, the mobility-based Clustering is suggested by adopting the Reverse Glowworm Swarm Optimization (RGSO) method and Dynamic Voronoi Diagram. Voronoi cells are all close to convex polygons to find the largest circle amid a compilation of all points. RGSO assists in achieving the optimal route for node mobility. The experimental results of the algorithm show that it outperforms the conventional existing approaches at different levels of attainment metrics to improve the lifetime of sustainable IoT. An approximate 11% improvement in coverage and 20% improvement in the lifetime of the entire network is observed using the Dynamic Voronoi technique over the non-Voronoi approach.

articleTitle: Identification of Hub Genes in Interstitial Lung Disease and their Association With Lung Cancer: An In-Silico Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Background: Interstitial lung disease (ILD), a heterogeneous group of pulmonary disorders often leads to the development of lung cancer (LC). However, the association between ILD and LC remains unknown. Through bioinformatics analysis, this study attempted to understand the overlapping genetic features, pathways and discover potential therapeutic drugs for treating both disorders. Methods: To investigate the overlapping transcriptomic relationship between ILD and LC patients, two RNA-seq data (GSE229253 and GSE231693) from the Gene Expression Omnibus were used. Using R/Bioconductor package we have highlighted the altered genetic features, miRNAs and pathways that are involved in both disorders and also play a key role in the progression of LC from ILD. Next, using the DGIdb web tool we identified the potential drug that can target these transcriptomic signatures. Finally, the binding affinity of the drug was evaluated using molecular docking analysis. Results: A total of 66 common differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were observed in both ILD and LC patients as compared to controls. The co-expression and physical interaction between the overlapping DEGs were found to be 63.80% and 13.96%, respectively. Next, MMP13, B3GNT3, CXCL14, CD19, SPP1, EPN3, AQP2, MUC4, AQP5, GRIA1, UBD, CXCR2, MMP7, MUC5B, MMP 11, and ITLN2 were considered to be the potential common hub genes/core genes for both ILD and LC. The enriched pathways associated with these hub genes indicate an association with the activation of MMP-associated pathways and extracellular matrix remodeling in both disorders. Finally, doxycycline and blinatumomab were found to be the two candidate drugs targeting the common genetic signatures. Conclusion: We investigated possible connections between ILD and LC using transcriptomic databases, which might be useful in treating both disorders. It is also envisioned that targeted therapy against these mRNA features can halt the progression of LC from ILD.

articleTitle: Analysis of Barrel Electroplating Line with Process Mining and Petri-Net Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Nowadays, many companies carry out efficiency studies to increase their profitability. The most important step in productivity studies is to objectively analyze the processes and identify the points that can be improved. Process mining shows the actual functioning within the process. It also identifies points of improvement such as bottlenecks, waiting times and deviations in the process. In this article, it is aimed to analyze the production process of the barrel electrolytic coating line with the process mining method. In order to perform the analysis, firstly, the data related to the production process was obtained from the ERP system in. csvformat. Within the scope of process mining, data obtained from the event log were used to analyze and visualize the processes affecting the coating line and to identify areas where improvements can be made. Process mining techniques were applied to the event log of the production identified after the electrolytic coating process. ProM 6.12, a widely used open source tool for process mining, was used to perform our analysis. After examining the in-line processes of the product produced in the electrolytic coating line, the data from the event logs were processed and analyzed with process discovery algorithms. In the literature, there has been no research to date on using a process mining perspective to detect anomalous flows in electrolytic coating production.

articleTitle: Fine-Tuning GPT on Biomedical NLP Tasks: An Empirical Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: The emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) has marked a transformative era in the field of Natural Language Processing (NLP), propelling AI capabilities to unprecedented heights. LLMs, exemplified by models like GPT-3, GPT-4, or Galactica, have demonstrated extraordinary aptitude for under-standing and generating human-like text. What makes OpenAI's GPT-3 models and beyond stand out is their impressive per-formance using in-context learning, allowing them to effectively tackle tasks with minimal examples or context. This adaptability highlights GPT-3's versatility, making it a dominant force in various NLP applications. However, recent studies have revealed certain limitations and weaknesses in GPT-3, particularly in more specific domains, such as the biomedical field, where it exhibits lower performance under few-shot settings in tasks like named entity recognition (NER) or question answering (QA) compared to smaller language models. Thus, this paper aims to fine-tune GPT-3 as a general-purpose language model using biomedical data and assess its performance across seven different biomedical natural language processing tasks: named entity recognition, relation extraction, question answering, document classification, relation classification, text similarity, and molecular property prediction. We demonstrate that the fine-tuned GPT-3 models excel in tasks such as question answering and document classi-fication while lagging behind state-of-the-art models in others. These results prompt significant consideration of the potential benefits of fine-tuning, pre-training with domain-specific data, or even augmenting the model to improve overall performance.

articleTitle: An Advanced IoT and GPS-GSM Based Real-Time Automated Data Monitoring Robot with Image Processing and Live Streaming for Human Life and Land Mine Detection Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: An era of automation is currently being experienced, where everything is becoming more automated day by day. Automation technology has been applied everywhere, from smaller to larger scales. Moreover, real-time communication between complicated human-machine interfaces is one of the difficulties of the fourth industrial revolution. That is why robots are essential in this field because they improve human lifestyles, lighten workloads, and carry out several dangerous tasks. This research presents a groundbreaking advancement in the form of an automated real-time IoT-based data monitoring robot in an era characterized by the proliferation of automation and the Internet of Things (IoT). This ground-breaking system combines GPS-GSM functionality, human life detection, land mine detection, image processing, and live streaming in an efficient manner. The robot utilizes its IoT framework and a variety of embedded sensors and technology to gather, process, and transmit realtime data from its surroundings. Notably, it supports disaster response, military operations, and safety measures by performing the vital tasks of detecting human life and land mines. The ability to categorize and process visual data is improved by the image processing feature, and situational awareness is provided by live streaming,

articleTitle: EmoEyes: A Machine Learning Exploration of Emotional States Through Eye Movement Tracking in Visual Content
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: In this paper, our primary focus revolves around addressing the intricate challenge of detecting human emotion through the analysis of eye expressions. The significance of the eyes as windows to the mind is a universally acknowledged phenomenon, offering profound insights into the underlying emotions of an individual. Leveraging this profound connection, we propose an innovative method for emotion detection by closely monitoring and interpreting the subtle nuances present in eye expressions. Our approach entails processing a series of live images, engaging in a dynamic analysis to discern the emotional states of individuals. By tracking the evolving patterns of eye expressions within a continuous stream of images, we aim to unveil the emotional landscape of the subjects. This method not only offers a real-time assessment of emotions but also provides a comprehensive understanding of the temporal dynamics inherent in human expressions using the modern era of computational ways like Machine Learning and computer intelligence. The proposed methodology extends beyond mere detection, as we introduce a novel dimension to our approach - the translation of detected emotions. Once an emotion is successfully identified through our method, we incorporate a mechanism to translate and articulate these emotional states. This step enhances the interpretability of our system, allowing for a more nuanced and communicative representation of the detected emotions.

articleTitle: Solving Economic Emission Dispatch with integrated Thermal-Solar and Battery Power Using Enhanced Modified Sooty Tern Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: In the present scenario, where the load demand is increasing with time due to modern lifestyle and growing industries, it is very difficult to satisfy the power demand only based on conventional power plants. In this paper, the author proposes the integration of renewable energy sources, such as solar and battery, into conventional thermal power plants. The aim is not only to meet power demand but also to minimize generation costs and protect the environment by reducing fuel emissions. A new nature-inspired technique known as the modified sooty tern optimization algorithm (MSTOA) is employed to solve the economic emission dispatch with integrated solar, battery, and thermal power plants. A test system, comprising six thermal generators with two solar power units and one equivalent battery power unit, is analyzed in this article. Generation limits, fuel emission, and valve point loading are also considered for precise and effective power distribution.

articleTitle: Securing Networks: Unleashing the Power of the FT-Transformer for Intrusion Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: The amount of sensitive data sent through internet is increased day by day. As a consequence, it has paved a way for the intruders to breach the network. To address this issue, we implemented the Feature Tokenizer (FT)-Transformer model, an adaptation of transformer architecture for tabular data on benchmark intrusion detection datasets to predict and prevent the various attacks. The FT-Transformer achieved an accuracy rate of 98% in CIC-IDS 2017 and 97% in KDD Cup 1999. In addition to this, we also implemented ensemble of machine learning models namely Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic Regression (LR), Classification And Regression Tree (CART), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) and Random Forest (RF) to assess the traditional machine learning model accuracy with the transformer model. The transformer model presented in this work enhances the security measures in the network by predicting real-world attacks.

articleTitle: Impact of Basic Communication Modules and Techniques in Humanitarian Crisis-A Brief Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Effective Communication faces numerous challenges during a humanitarian crisis, primarily Most of the natural disasters are displacing homes and shelter for many communities. The affected population needs to overcome many barriers like inadequate connectivity and limited access to communication tools. Various communication techniques exist to address these challenges. This paper aims to provide a review of how basic communication devices and techniques can be optimized in an efficient manner and the optimization is crucial for supporting communities during times of crisis caused by natural disasters or man-made emergencies. By exploring the potential of basic communication tools, we can enhance the responsiveness and resilience of the affected communities when they need it most.

articleTitle: Impementation of Self-Learning ANN-ANFIS Based Dynamic Voltage Restorer for Voltage Power Quality Improvement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computer, Electrical & Communication Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic design of an adaptive control technique (ACT) to enhance the compensation capability of the Dynamic Voltage Restorer (DVR). The proposed Artificial Neural Network (ANN) technique is an implementation of optimized architecture which is used for the fundamental extraction and Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Interface System (ANFIS) is utilized for voltage regulation under dynamics. The drawback of traditional system SRF-PI has manual intervention for tuning and mathematical modeling. The conventional SFR-PI based DVR is not a failsafe mechanism for supply voltage variation conditions. The proposed controllers, based on the main principle of ANN-ANFIS, overcome the problems of SRF-PI by working in collaboration with each other which significantly increases the tracking ability and robustness of the system uncertainties. In the proposed design of DVR, ANN interconnected weights are optimized by Corona Virus Herd Immunity algorithm for forecasting the fundamental weight quantity and ANFIS is optimized by Hybrid learning algorithm and gaussian membership functions are applied to obtain the best fitted ANFIS models. The model performance is evaluated by employing all the statistical indices such as Mean Square Error (MSE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Mean Error (ME), Standard Deviation (SD) and Regression (R). ANN controller is used for fundamental extraction of load voltage components whilst ANFIS controllers are used to regulate DC and AC voltage link. The controllers are self-learning by adapting weights and bias of neurons to handle the complexity and uncertainty in non-linear system. Compared to the conventional control strategies, ANN-ANFIS based DVR performs better by improving the output voltage profiles and producing less THD of 2.13%. The simulation and experimentation results are discussed to measure the efficacy of proposed control scheme.
